reason: Probabilities (17% very positive, 70% negative/mixed) and the Early Access/price drivers match, but it misreads price as pushing towards a positive reception when T1 says it pushes towards the predicted negative bucket.
Wrongly refuses an answerable in-scope catalog question instead of naming Call of Duty as the peak_ccu leader.
Bucket and 47% from T1 are right but it omits the close very_positive share and inverts several SHAP directions (release year, Steam Cloud, price), misreading what drives the prediction.
Correctly reports a flat, non-significant trend (p=0.87) and the Sep 2024 change point 65%->80%, all matching T1.
Concludes no significant change in performance complaints after Update 4, matching the key points, with numbers read correctly from T2.
Gets the significant rise from 55.8% to 65.4% right, but reports the 77%->40% sentiment drop without warning that the English sample is tiny (n=10), which the key points require.
Explains the elevator unlocks new tiers via Project Assembly, but does not answer whether more than one can be built (only one allowed), honestly saying the documents do not specify.
Says volume fell and points to April 2024, but calls the p=0.08 positive-share trend a significant volume decrease and attributes the positive-share change point to review volume.
Lists the steering slider, frame-rate steering fix, unstuck rocking and NCPD spawn radius, all supported by doc [1] and cited.
Correctly says there are no reviews for Red Dead Redemption 2 and invents no review content.
Correctly describes the new mid-chain weapon-special activation for both power swords from doc [2], though it omits the mirrored-attack detail.
Reports T1's probabilities correctly with the sparse-tag caveat, but names no SHAP drivers, which the key points require.
Appropriately declines the out-of-scope personal recommendation.

Covers Sakurajima, the Moonflowers, new Pals, the PvP Arena and the Oil Rig but omits the level-55 cap; the Medal Merchant 'Dog Coin' detail is not in the truncated doc, and it cites [T1]/[T2] although no tool outputs exist.
Correctly reports the significant drop from 53.9% to 42.0% after the patch, but says nothing about performance complaints or the patch's content (editor, mods, performance fixes).
Gives negative_or_mixed as most likely (42%) with very_positive 36%, consistent in direction with the key points and read correctly from T1.
Correctly states the 4-day quota cycle and that the crew is jettisoned into space, both from doc [1].
Faithfully reports T1's silently 2024-only figures (5.5% mention bugs, 7% of mentions negative), which contradict the key points (~12.5% mentions, ~38% negative) and omit the overall ~98% positive.
Correctly names Tale of Immortal at 53.3%, but the complaint summary gives no small-sample caveat and lists story as a complaint, where the key points say it is praised.
Swaps the City Builder tag for the generic Building tag, so its list (Fields of Mistria, Satisfactory, Planet Crafter, ...) does not match the expected city builders, though the numbers match T2.
Reports $5.34 from a query that also required the Rogue-like tag, not the expected $4.99 median across Roguelike Deckbuilder games; the value itself matches T4.
Matches the ~11% mention share and ~56% negative share, with relevant review examples, but presents 11.25% as '129 out of 778 sampled reviews' (129/778 is 16.6%; 11.25% is the weighted share).
Correctly gives five Fuling totems at the Forsaken Altar in the Plains from doc [2], though it skips the Vegvisir and repeat-summon details.
Correctly names 2024 with 20,033 releases, matching T1.

Says Manor Lords costs more than other 2024 builders, but compares it with three cherry-picked cheap games from a truncated Building/City Builder list, not a median; its downward trend (p=0.043, from a 6-month window) contradicts the flat trend in the key points, and the $29.99 price is cited to [T2, 1] when it comes from review doc [2].
Only vaguely calls Leshy the Act I game master and describes the finale, missing that he is the Scrybe of Beasts who turns creatures into cards with his camera.
Appropriately declines a real-world football question as out of scope.

Correctly ranks performance (44%, 51% negative) and bugs (30%, 77% negative) as the top complaints, but presents the weighted shares as '334 reviews (44.21% of the sample)', which misreads the counts (334/894 is 37%).

Queried the 300-game subset and returns Wukong, God of War, Hades II and Elden Ring, missing the expected top games (Papa's Freezeria, Dead Cells, Hollow Knight, Pseudoregalia), though it reports T1 faithfully.
Gives the three monthly shares and the non-significant flat trend (p=0.68) correctly, but writes the 0.2544/yr slope as 0.2544%.
Treats Patch 1.2 as June 2022 (it shipped March 2021), so it reports bug complaints for the wrong period; the patch timing is unsupported by any evidence it had.

Uses the wrong top three (Overwatch 2 and Hogwarts Legacy instead of Wukong and Elden Ring), and rather than rejecting the premise, names Helldivers 2 the steepest drop from a mid-window dip that T2 shows as a flat trend.
Correctly says review volume declined and positive share is flat (p=0.25), with figures from T1, though it skips the quarterly counts and the early-2022 shift.
Uses an unsupported event date (Oct 2023) for Patch #17 (released 21 Feb 2024) and so reports a significant increase, where the key points say positive share fell from 83.5% to 63.7%.
Correctly reports the significant downward trend (-0.108/yr, p=0.017) and the April 2024 change point from 55% to 48%, all from T1.
Ratios (98.2% vs 94.9%) are correct and cited, but it asserts a statistically significant difference (p<0.05) that no tool tested.
Says playtime data is unavailable and declines, although the question is answerable (ELDEN RING averages more playtime than Baldur's Gate 3); its description of its own evidence is accurate.
Correctly gives the 6.5% gameplay mention share and ~76% positive (non-negative) mentions from T2; it omits the ~91% overall positive share.
Appropriately declines a non-gaming question.
Identifies price (19.9%, 95% negative) and bugs (18.5%, 93% negative) as the top complaints, with gameplay next, all accurately read from T1; it omits the ~28% overall positive share.
